source_title: My Hero Academia: 6 Strongest Versions of Shoto Todoroki, Ranked
source_excerpt:
Cathlyn is an anime writer with years of experience covering some of the biggest and most popular series of all time. She loves writing listicles, features, and query-based articles about all things related to anime. Outside of writing, she enjoys playing mobile games, building Lego and Nanoblock sets, playing pickleball, watching movies, and rewatching her favorite anime series. Before joining GameRant as a contributor, she worked in Epicstream’s anime department. Beyond her passion for anime, she also enjoys writing romance fiction, with her most successful work surpassing one million reads on Wattpad.
Shoto Todoroki has one of the most unique abilities in My Hero Academia . Equipped with a versatile Quirk that allows him to use both fire and ice in combat, Shoto can unleash many different offensive and defensive combinations that overwhelm his enemies in unimaginable ways.
From the beginning of My Hero Academia , Shoto is a prodigy whose natural talent grants him easy access to increasingly powerful versions of himself. By embracing his Half-Cold Half-Hot Quirk physically and emotionally, Shoto eventually transforms into a powerful hero capable of surpassing his rivals.
6 World Heroes' Mission Shoto Overcomes Leviathan With Flashfire Fist: Jet Kindling
In My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission , Shoto faces Leviathan, a powerful rampage villain working with the Humarise cult. He is capable of controlling and extending the appendages on his fingers and head with his Helical Scythe Quirk. The formidable opponent, enhanced by the Trigger drug, pushes Shoto onto the defensive, nearly drowning him before unleashing an incredibly dangerous torrent of fire that burns the young hero.
At this point, Shoto still has much to learn before surpassing Endeavor, but that doesn't mean he cannot defeat formidable opponents like Leviathan. By combining his fire and ice abilities, Shoto freezes the villain before unleashing a Flashfreeze Heatwave attack. Although Leviathan manages to withstand the initial assault, Shoto follows up with Flashfire Fist: Jet Kindling , concentrating his flames at their highest possible intensity to finally defeat the villain.
5 Paranormal Liberation War Shoto Faces Three of My Hero Academia's Most Dangerous Villains
Fresh from his Hero Work Studies, Shoto faces one of his toughest challenges in My Hero Academia . Although he has improved his speed under Endeavor's training, learned to use his fire abilities to propel himself through the air, and received an upgraded costume, his sudden confrontation with Dabi leaves him with severe burns. It goes without saying that this version of Shoto still needs more improvement to keep up with Dabi.
Even so, Shoto delivers an impressive performance during the Paranormal Liberation War, outperforming many heroes by helping protect his allies against the combined threats of Tomura Shigaraki, Gigantomachia, and Dabi. From cooling Endeavor's overheated body and teaming up with Nejire Hado to rescuing Izuku and Bakugo and withstanding Dabi's Jet Burn attack, Shoto proves himself to be an invaluable asset during the Paranormal Liberation War.
4 Shoto Todoroki's Full Power Is on Display in My Hero Academia: You're Next Movie
Shoto's impressive combat performance with Izuku and Bakugo in the My Hero Academia: You're Next movie deserves recognition, as he defeats multiple villains, including those capable of teleportation and telekinesis, as well as an opponent with a heavily modified alchemy quirk.
Alongside Bakugo and Izuku, Shoto shows off his full power through his Flashfreeze Heatwave ultimate move, unleashing a devastating combination of ice and fire that significantly weakens Dark Might. Unfortunately, Shoto's quirk is incompatible with Anna Scervino's Quirk overmodification, depriving fans of the chance to see him wield an even more powerful version of his Quirk.
3 Pre-Final War Shoto Learns to Combine Fire and Ice Into One Power
Before heading into his final battle with Dabi, Pre-Final War Shoto finally achieves the perfect balance between both sides of his Quirk, allowing him to harness his ice and fire abilities in harmony. This crucial breakthrough leads to the official creation of Phosphor, Shoto's version of Flashfire Fist technique that combines both halves of his quirk into a single, devastating power.
At this point, however, Shoto was still training to master Phosphor, as maintaining the technique for prolonged periods proved challenging. The technique can be uncontrollable, after all. He also struggled to incorporate it into his ultimate moves, requiring further practice to fully integrate its power into his improved fighting style.
2 Final War Shoto Counters Dabi's Superior Flames
With help from his family, Shoto emerges victoriously in his battle against Dabi during the Final War. Despite Dabi's superior Blueflame Quirk , Final War Shoto masterfully combines his Quirk with Flashfire Fist: Phosphor to extinguish his brother's flames and put an end to his thirst for revenge. Shoto would never have achieved this feat if he hadn't realized that weaker flames alone were insufficient to counter Dabi's superior Blueflame.
Eventually, Shoto uses Great Glacial Aegir, an incredibly powerful ultimate move that unleashes a massive wave of freezing flames against Dabi. When Final War Shoto uses the technique a second time, its increased power allows him to suppress Dabi's near-explosive flames and prevent a catastrophic blast. That's not all, as the wave of cold fire completely covered the surrounding terrain in ice.
1 Pro Hero Shoto Is Finding New Ways to Further Master His Quirk
At present, Shoto Todoroki ranks Pro-Hero No. 2 , second only to Lemillion in the Hero Billboard Chart. Although this version of Shoto has no actual feats, it's safe to assume that he has grown significantly stronger since the Final War. Shoto has most likely refined his Half-Hot, Half-Cold Quirk to bring both his ice and fire abilities together in a way that maximizes his full power.
For now, Shoto leads the Endeavor Agency, helping the public recognize him on his own merits rather than his father's legacy. He remains one of Japan's most popular heroes and maintains a close friendship with Izuku and Bakugo, both of whom have stood beside him through some of his most challenging battles. At this point, it wouldn't be a surprise if he eventually surpasses Lemillion and becomes Japan's top hero.
